newsitem.title: UK: Lufthansa says MD-11 to cut cargo unit cost 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa says MD-11 to cut cargo unit cost 10 pct.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said the five new McDonnell Douglas MD-11 long-range trijets it is buying will cut its unit costs by more than 10 percent due to lower fuel, maintenance and crew costs.

"Unit costs will come down by more than 10 percent," Lufthansa board member Klaus Nittinger told a news conference at the Farnborough air show after the airline announced it had agreed to buy five MD-11Fs and take out options on seven more.
"The long range of the aircraft will help us to avoid hubs which will speed up transport and save a lot of costs in future," said Lufthansa Cargo chairman William Althen.
"The fuel burn per weight unit is 30 to 40 percent lower (than the Boeing 747-200 it currently flies), which is a huge advantage when fuel prices are increasing," he said.

Nevertheless Althen said the airline would keep its fleet of 11 Boeing 747-200 freighters and operate them in conjuction with the MD-11Fs for the next 10 or 15 years. The MD-11F has a crew of two, one less than the 747s.

"The only way to stay in the market is to bring down costs. With the 747-200 there's no chance of doing so in future," Althen said, saying possible routes for the MD-11Fs included the U.S. west coast, South America, Singapore and Hong Kong.
